blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A transformer's load must stay at or below 80 unless a spare unit is rented (binary r). The model writes load <= 80 + 15 r. In plans the other rows allow, the load can reach 100. What does this model do?

options.text: Refuses every plan with a load above 95, even with the spare rented
options.says: Right: with r = 1 the row still says load <= 95, so an M of 15 is too small and plans the rule allows are refused.

options.text: Allows every plan with the spare rented, since r switches the row off
options.says: The row is only off when M covers the largest load; 15 does not cover 100 - 80.

options.text: Reports the model infeasible, since M is smaller than the load needs
options.says: Plans with smaller loads are still allowed; the model quietly returns a worse plan, and no status says so.

options.text: Allows loads up to 95 without the spare, since M always adds to the limit
options.says: With r = 0 the term 15 r is 0, so the limit is 80.

origin.section: A Switched Row Is Off Only When M Covers the Largest Value Its Left Side Can Take

questions.stem: A row 3u - 2v <= 10 must be switched off by a binary h. The variables have bounds 0 <= u <= 6 and 1 <= v <= 4, and no other row is used. What is the smallest M the bounds justify?

options.text: M = 16, the largest value 3u - 2v can take
options.says: M is the most the left side can exceed the right side, so 10 is subtracted.

options.text: M = 0, with u at its upper bound and v at its upper bound
options.says: A negative coefficient makes its term largest at the variable's lower bound, not its upper bound.

options.text: M = 6, with u at its upper bound and v at its lower bound
M = 8, with u at its upper bound and the v term left out
options.says: Every term counts at its own best case; v's best case is -2, not 0.

origin.section: Variable Bounds Give a Safe M With No Solve

questions.stem: For one crew row, the bounds give M = 40, the LP maximum of the left side less the right side is 23.6, and the MILP maximum is 21. The left side is a whole number in every plan. Which values of M are valid?

options.text: Only 21, since any larger M would refuse some allowed plan
options.says: A larger M is always safe; it only weakens the LP bound.

options.text: 21, 23 and 40, since each is at least the MILP maximum
options.says: Right: every valid M covers the MILP maximum, and the LP value may be rounded down to 23 because the left side is whole.

options.text: Only 40, since the LP and MILP values never count the bounds
options.says: Each rule uses more of the model than the one before, bounds included, and all of them are valid.

options.text: Only 21 and 40, since 23 is always below the LP maximum
options.says: With a whole-number left side the LP value can be rounded down: no plan reaches 23.6, so none exceeds 23.
